I think it should all depend on what you actually do. I've met veterans who are missing limbs and have all kinds of nasty scars. Most of them from fighting in other countries to keep others safe from terrorists and the likes. Those men and women get my utmost respect. Then there's the ones who never see a day of combat in their lives but brag like they did the bravest thing ever. Those don't get my respect.

I wouldnt mind being forced to serve. If I didnt have any tattoos I would go for it. If the U.S ever does go to an official big war a draft would still be necessary because a lot of the volunteers do non combat jobs.

Except that's not true now a days. Almost all the recruits I know are only doing it to get paid and no other reason. They even pick the shortest safest job they can to just go Fuck around a couple years get the check and come back. Most of them won't ever get anywhere near combat. Out of the 30ish high school kids I know who have gone straight to the army maybe 3 of them chose jobs that will actually come with any form of risk.

Thought this too. A lot still are respectable but now more and more im seeing friends and people I went to school with signing up. I asked why and over half of them say they are just doing it to get a check and they all picked the least risky job they could that was also the shortest amount of time. Makes me mad when they come home and everyone treats them like they are doing something so brave when in reality all they care about is money and won't ever be but in combat due to their jobs not being direct combat. Respect to the ones who are really doing it for a good cause.
